# @moku-labs/native

> Node-only native packager framework for Moku, built on @moku-labs/core: it generates a gitignored Tauri 2 project, codegens the permission surface (capabilities JSON, Info.ios.plist sidecar, AndroidManifest needs) from whichever system plugins the app composed, and runs `tauri build` for five targets (macos, windows, linux, ios, android).

## Core Concepts

### Three-layer Moku model
- Layer 1 (`src/config.ts`): `createCoreConfig<Config, Events, [logPlugin, envPlugin]>("native", { config, plugins, pluginConfigs: { env: { providers: [workerSafeProcessEnv()] } } })` — global Config + Events types, shared constants (`TARGETS`, `PHASE_ORDER`), the `hostTargets()` helper, the shared `MobileTarget`/`TauriRunner`/`BuildFlavor`/`BuildProfile` types, and the two `@moku-labs/common` core plugins so every plugin ctx carries `ctx.log` and `ctx.env`. The env provider is seeded HERE: without it `ctx.env.get("PATH")` is undefined and the tauri plugin cannot PATH-walk `node`.
- Layer 2 (`src/index.ts`): `createCore(coreConfig, { plugins: [projectPlugin, tauriPlugin, buildPlugin, doctorPlugin, cliPlugin] })` — the framework. NO pluginConfigs block: every plugin's defaults live in its own `src/plugins/<name>/index.ts`.
- Layer 3 (consumer): `createApp({ config, plugins?, pluginConfigs? })` — a consumer app instance with `native.project/.tauri/.build/.doctor/.cli` APIs plus `native.start()`/`native.stop()`.

### The composition is the permission surface
`config.system` is a name-only array (`ReadonlyArray<{ name: string }>`). The project plugin resolves each name against an 8-row capability registry (store, notification, clipboard-manager, tray, deep-link, back, haptics, shell) into npm/crate dependency ranges, cargo features, Rust plugin-init lines, capability permission JSON, tauri.conf fragments, and per-platform applicability. Unknown names throw at composition time (project.onInit). `tray` is a CORE TAURI CARGO FEATURE (`tray-icon`), not a plugin: its row has no crate, no npm package and no rust init, which is why every plugin-shaped `RegistryRow` field is optional while `cargoFeatures` is required. tray's permissions are `["core:tray:default", "core:menu:default", "core:image:default", "core:resources:default", "core:app:allow-default-window-icon"]`: `@moku-labs/system` defaults the tray icon to `defaultWindowIcon()`, whose command is NOT in `core:default`, so without the last id a real macOS shell fails with `Command plugin:app|default_window_icon not allowed by ACL`; the menu/image/resources ids are already inside `core:default` and are listed anyway so the row documents the full surface. `back` is core permissions alone (`["core:app:allow-exit"]`, Android only, no crate/npm/init; `onBackButtonPress` + `exit` ship in `@tauri-apps/api/app`) — `exit` and its permission exist since tauri 2.12.0, so the generated Cargo.toml pins `tauri = { version = "2.12", … }`. `haptics` is `tauri-plugin-haptics`/`@tauri-apps/plugin-haptics` `^2`, init `tauri_plugin_haptics::init()`, iOS + Android only, and names its four commands (`haptics:allow-impact-feedback`, `haptics:allow-notification-feedback`, `haptics:allow-selection-feedback`, `haptics:allow-vibrate`) because the plugin ships no default set. Mobile permission codegen is conf-only (D-012): no permission XML is patched; official Tauri plugins self-merge their own AndroidManifest needs (haptics merges VIBRATE itself); the one XML the packager writes is presentation — `app.orientation` (`"portrait"` → iOS `UISupportedInterfaceOrientations` = [Portrait], `~ipad` = [Portrait, PortraitUpsideDown], `UIRequiresFullScreen` = true, Android `android:screenOrientation="portrait"`; `"landscape"` → both iOS keys = [LandscapeLeft, LandscapeRight] + `UIRequiresFullScreen`, Android `"sensorLandscape"`; `"any"`/unset → no iOS keys and the Android attribute REMOVED). On iOS `src-tauri/Info.ios.plist` is ALWAYS written (an empty `<dict>` when nothing is locked) because the writer never deletes and Tauri merges it on every build; other targets get none. `app.backgroundColor` → `app.windows[0].backgroundColor`, and on Android it also styles the status bar: the patch pass rewrites the generated MainActivity.kt `enableEdgeToEdge()` call to `SystemBarStyle.dark(Color.TRANSPARENT)` (light icons) when the colour's relative luminance is below 0.179, else `SystemBarStyle.light(Color.TRANSPARENT, Color.TRANSPARENT)` (dark icons); unset restores the bare call. The same colour also paints the Android window and the Android 12+ icon splash: the pass writes `res/values/moku_window_background.xml` and adds marked `android:windowBackground` + `android:windowSplashScreenBackground` items (both `@color/moku_window_background`) to the manifest's app theme in every `res/values*/themes.xml`, so no dark frame shows between the icon splash and the first paint; unset removes them and the colour file. deep-link is custom-scheme-only (D-011: `{ mode: "scheme", scheme }`) and resolves to `{ desktop: { schemes: [s] }, mobile: [{ scheme: [s], appLink: false }] }`. deep-link is also the ONLY row that gets a `plugins.<name>` key in tauri.conf.json: store/notification/clipboard-manager take no config, their Tauri plugin deserializes `unit`, and an empty `{}` map under their key aborts the app at startup (`invalid type: map, expected unit`), so a capability with an empty resolved conf contributes no key. `app.adaptiveIconInset` (percent per side of the 108 dp canvas, `0 < n ≤ 30`, validated; `19.44` keeps full-bleed art in the 66 dp safe zone) wraps the Android launcher foreground in `res/mipmap-anydpi-v26/ic_launcher.xml` + `ic_launcher_round.xml` in an `<inset>`; `project.patchMobileIcons({ target })` applies it after `tauri icon` on EVERY android build (tauri icon rewrites those files); unset restores the plain foreground.

### The shell capability (Android page bridge)
`shell` is the one row backed by a crate this framework GENERATES: `localCrate: { name: "tauri-plugin-moku-shell", directory: "plugins/moku-shell" }` (under projectDir, linked by path, never published), `rustInit: "tauri_plugin_moku_shell::init()"`, permission `moku-shell:default`, no npm package, `platforms: ["android"]` (iOS deferred, Decision D6: filtered out like any platform-limited row), confidence medium. A row has `crate` + `crateRange` OR `localCrate`, never both. Composed like every capability — `system: [{ name: "shell" }]`; `capabilities.shell` is `Record<string, never>` and composes nothing alone. The debug profile composes it on android even unnamed. Its init script runs before page scripts, in the main frame, and installs a frozen `globalThis.__MOKU_NATIVE__` (contract v1; a browser, iOS or an app without the shell has none):
```ts
type MokuNative = {
  version: 1; platform: "android";
  build: { profile: "debug" | "release"; id: string }; // id "<app.version>+<app.buildNumber ?? 0>", "-debug" suffix in debug
  device: { model: string; manufacturer: string; sdk: number } | null; // null until `ready`
  ready: Promise<void>;                                // never rejects
  display: { maxHz: number | null; setFrameRate(fps: number | null): Promise<{ panelHz: number | null; maxHz: number | null }> };
  thermal: { read(): Promise<{ status: "none" | "light" | "moderate" | "severe" | "critical" | "emergency" | "shutdown"; headroom: number | null; at: number; android?: { status: number; headroom: number | null; forecastSeconds: 10 } }> };
  insets: { readonly current: { top: number; right: number; bottom: number; left: number } }; // CSS px
  share?(file: { name: string; mime: string; bytes: Uint8Array }): Promise<{ shared: boolean }>; // debug only, ≤ 32 MiB
};
```
Insets also land as `--moku-device-safe-top|right|bottom|left` on `document.documentElement.style` (pages read `var(--moku-safe-top, var(--moku-device-safe-top, env(safe-area-inset-top)))`, so a page's own `--moku-safe-*` rule wins) and dispatch `moku-native:insets` on `window`; thermal status changes dispatch `moku-native:thermal`. In debug, `console.log|info|warn|error|debug` also reach logcat under tag `moku-page` (≤ 4000 chars). WebView origin of the packaged page: Android and Windows `http://tauri.localhost`; iOS, macOS, Linux `tauri://localhost`. `project.checkShellLinked({ target, profile })` runs after the compile and fails when the shell is composed but `gen/android/tauri.settings.gradle` does not name `moku-shell` (tree initialised before the shell existed → clean android and rebuild).

### The two-createApp consumer shape (D-009)
A native app is a SEPARATE `createApp` (e.g. `src/native.ts`) composed BESIDE the consumer's web/node app — plugins are bound to their own framework's factory chain, so native plugins can never join the web app's plugin array. Integration happens at the edges:
- `src/system.ts` — the shared array of `{ name }` system-plugin declarations; both apps import it; it is the cross-team contract.
- package.json wires thin per-verb consumer scripts (`native:build`, `native:dev`, `native:doctor`, `native:clean`), each a small file that does `await native.start(); await native.cli.<verb>(...); await native.stop();` — there is no argv CLI.
- Directory roles: `projectDir` (default `.moku/tauri/`) = the generated, GITIGNORED, fully regenerable Tauri project (contains `src-tauri/`); `outDir` (default `dist-native/`) = final packaged artifacts per target (`dist-native/<target>/`).

### Pipeline and events
`build.run({ target })` walks `PHASE_ORDER` = scaffold → codegen → icons → compile → bundle → collect, sequentially, stopping at the first failing phase. `build.prepare({ target })` runs the first three and stops (cli.dev calls it first). It emits the GLOBAL framework events `native:phase` (start/progress/done/error per phase) and `native:complete` (on success) — declared in `src/config.ts` (D-003), emitted by build, hooked by cli for live rendering, hookable by any plugin without a depends edge. `doctor:check` stays a per-plugin event (declared by doctor; hooking it needs a `depends: [doctorPlugin]` edge) and is emitted per check AS IT SETTLES. codegen owns the mobile story: generate → `tauri.mobileInit({ target })` when completeness is `not-initialized` → completeness gate → idempotent `project.patchMobile({ target, runner: tauri.getRunner() })`. The icons phase is real: `project.ensureIconSource()` (config `app.icon` or a generated placeholder PNG) then `tauri.icon({ source })`, skipped only when `src-tauri/icons/icon.png` exists, the `src-tauri/icons/.source` stamp beside it (absolute source path + size + mtime) still describes the current source, AND mobileInit did not just run — an mtime comparison alone would miss `app.icon` switching to an OLDER file. compile opens with `project.clearMobileBuildOutput({ target })` for ios ONLY (removes `gen/apple/build`, else `tauri ios build` fails the second build of a tree with `Directory not empty`); something removed → one compile `progress` event with detail `cleared previous build output`, a refusal there is a compile error and `tauri.build` never starts. compile+bundle share ONE `tauri build` subprocess; the transition is LIVE (first output line matching /bundling/i closes compile and opens bundle) and a failure is attributed to whichever phase is open. `BuildResult.phases` always carries six entries.

### Build profiles (debug on Android and iOS, dev)
`BuildFlavor.debug` (on `cli.build`, `build.run`, `build.runAll`; `build.prepare` takes `{ target, debug? }`) selects `BuildProfile` `"debug"` (unset = `"store"`; the page sees `"store"` as `"release"`). The debug profile is still a RELEASE build type (Rust + Gradle optimized, Decision D1) that installs BESIDE the store app: `generate({ target, profile })` composes the shell on android even unnamed; `patchMobile({ target, runner, profile })` writes a `// MOKU-PROFILE-START … END` Gradle block with `applicationIdSuffix = ".debug"`, renames `app_name`/`main_activity_title` to `"<app.name> (debug)"`, signs with the SDK debug keystore `<HOME ?? USERPROFILE>/.android/debug.keystore` (alias `androiddebugkey`, public `android` passwords; missing → `[native] debug keystore not found at <path>.` + the `keytool` command), and writes a cleartext `res/xml/network_security_config.xml` pointed at by `<application android:networkSecurityConfig>`. The store profile reverts every one of those byte for byte. The page gets `build.profile === "debug"`, console → logcat `moku-page`, WebView debugging, `share`. compile spawns tauri with `env: { MOKU_NATIVE_PROFILE: profile }` so the web build (run inside `tauri build`) can tell the profiles apart. At the end of compile/bundle, before collect: on android `project.checkShellLinked`, then `project.detectPageAgent()` — a STORE build (any target) whose `web.dist` `.js` files carry the editor agent (`"/__editor/hello"` or `"[moku-editor]"`) fails with `[native] store build refused: the page carries the editor agent (<dist>/<file>).` / `Build with debug: true.`; a debug build passes. collect delivers a debug build to `<outDir>/<target>-debug/` (so `dist-native/android-debug/`), never over the store installer. `BuildResult.profile` and `native:complete.profile` carry the profile; cli's completion panel prints `debug build → <outPath>`. `debug` on any target but android and ios throws `[native] --debug builds Android and iOS only for now (asked for <target>).` before any phase (no event); `runAll` checks every target up front and refuses the whole run.

`debug` on iOS (N4): the sidecar gains `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription` and `NSAppTransportSecurity { NSAllowsLocalNetworking: true }` after `ios.infoPlist`, the main window `devtools: true` and the `tauri` crate the `devtools` feature (Safari Web Inspector; iOS stays a release build). Native renames nothing on iOS: the engine passes the `.debug` id, the name and its own `projectDir`. `tauri ios build` merges the sidecar into `gen/apple/<slug>_iOS/Info.plist` for good, so the iOS patch pass outside the debug profile removes those two keys there. The shell stays Android only.

`BuildFlavor.dev` selects `BuildProfile` `"dev"`: the store profile (release signing with the game's key, no `.debug`, cleartext closed, `.aab` and `exportMethod` as asked, delivery to `<outDir>/<target>/`, the page reads `"release"`) except that an agent page is not refused, `MOKU_NATIVE_PROFILE=dev` reaches the web build, and `removeUnusedCommands` is absent. `dev` and `debug` together throw `[native] debug and dev cannot be combined.` before any phase. The config names the test app (id, name, icon, `projectDir`, `outDir`); native renames nothing.

### Seams and conventions
- `tauri` is the ONLY plugin that spawns processes (invocation: explicit PATH-walked `node` + `require.resolve("@tauri-apps/cli/tauri.js")` — never `bunx tauri`, never `process.execPath` which is bun; D-013). `tauri.getRunner()` exposes that pair so the generated Xcode/Android build phase can be rewritten to it.
- Every subprocess output line is scrubbed before reaching any log, callback, or error: known secret env-var names (quoted values captured whole), URL userinfo, standalone hex runs of 32+ chars, then Shannon-entropy gating. A location-shaped token is scanned PART by part (the runs between `-`, `.` and `#`), so a secret inside a path is masked while ordinary build names glued to a hash — `libtauri_app-<hash>.rlib`, `DerivedData/<name>-<hash>/`, `main-<hash>.css` — stay readable; UUIDs, the cargo `index.crates.io-<hash>` segment, and digests announced by `commit `/`rev `/a `git+<url>#` fragment/`checksum = "` stay readable too (a bare `#` is NOT enough).
- Signing config carries env-var REFERENCES and identifiers only; doctor checks presence (`ctx.env.has`) and counts, never values.
- All CLI output flows through the branded kit `@moku-labs/common/cli` (MC1); logging via `ctx.log` (MC2); env via `ctx.env` (MC3).
- Dev teardown is owned by the tauri dev seam's own control flow (process-group spawn, SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers, `DevHandle.stop()`) — there is no `onStop` (D-002); cli awaits the handle but never holds or stops it.
- `project` owns `clean` (D-006); `cli.clean` is a thin delegate, confirm-gated when wiping the whole projectDir. `assertCleanableRoot` (and, at composition time, `validate.ts` for `projectDir`) applies POSITIVE containment from `paths.ts`: the resolved (realpath, NFC, case-insensitive on darwin/win32) root must sit strictly inside the PROJECT ANCHOR or a usable OS temp root, and must not be — or contain — the anchor, the cwd or `$HOME`, nor be a filesystem root. The anchor is the nearest ancestor of the cwd with a `.git` entry or a `workspaces` package.json, stopping before `$HOME`/the fs root (falls back to cwd) — an absolute `projectDir` at a monorepo root validates from `packages/app`. A temp root that is a filesystem root or that is/contains `$HOME` grants nothing (`TMPDIR`). `outDir` gets the looser `isDeliveryPath` rule (never recursively cleaned): only a filesystem root, `$HOME`, or an ancestor of the cwd/`$HOME` is refused. `build`'s collect guard borrows the same comparison through `project.resolveDerivedPath`.

## Quick Reference

```ts
import {
  createApp, createPlugin,            // framework API (Layer 3 factory + consumer plugin factory)
  projectPlugin, tauriPlugin, buildPlugin, doctorPlugin, cliPlugin,
  TARGETS, PHASE_ORDER, hostTargets,  // constants + host-target helper
  TauriError,                         // the one runtime value from a plugin (namespaces are type-only)
  type Config, type Events, type Target, type NativePhase,
  type NativePhaseEvent, type NativeCompleteEvent,
  type CapabilityConfigMap, type SigningConfig, type AppleSigning, type AppleExportMethod,
  type MobileTarget, type TauriRunner, type BuildFlavor, type BuildProfile, type Orientation,
  type Project, type Tauri, type Build, type Doctor, type Cli  // TYPE-ONLY namespaces
} from "@moku-labs/native";

// Layer 3
const native = createApp({
  config: { app, web, system, capabilities, targets, projectDir, outDir, signing },
  plugins: [],        // optional consumer-authored plugins
  pluginConfigs: { tauri: {...}, doctor: {...}, cli: {...} }
});
await native.start();

// cli verbs (typed methods, no argv parsing)
native.cli.build(opts?: { target?: Target; all?: boolean; simulator?: boolean; aab?: boolean; debug?: boolean; dev?: boolean }): Promise<void>; // debug: Android and iOS; dev: store-signed test build; never both
native.cli.dev(opts?: { target?: Target }): Promise<void>;      // prepares first; resolves on clean/signal exit
native.cli.doctor(opts?: { target?: Target }): Promise<boolean>; // caller sets process.exitCode
native.cli.clean(opts?: { target?: Target }): Promise<void>;    // no target => confirm-gated full wipe

// build pipeline
native.build.prepare(opts: { target: Target; debug?: boolean }): Promise<void>;  // scaffold + codegen + icons only
native.build.run(opts: { target: Target; simulator?: boolean; aab?: boolean; debug?: boolean }): Promise<Build.BuildResult>;
native.build.runAll(opts?: { targets?: readonly Target[]; simulator?: boolean; aab?: boolean; debug?: boolean }): Promise<readonly Build.BuildResult[]>; // sequential, never Promise.all

// project (files only, never spawns)
native.project.generate(opts: { target: Target; profile?: BuildProfile }): Promise<{ written: string[]; unchanged: string[]; skipped: string[] }>; // profile default "store"
native.project.getBundleLayout(opts: { target: Target }): BundleLayout; // { root, formats, genDirectory } — collect globs against it
native.project.getCompleteness(opts: { target: Target }): Project.CompletenessResult; // "not-applicable" | "not-initialized" | "incomplete" | "complete"
native.project.patchMobile(opts: { target: MobileTarget; runner?: TauriRunner; profile?: BuildProfile }): Promise<{ patched: readonly string[]; unchanged: readonly string[] }>;
native.project.patchMobileIcons(opts: { target: MobileTarget }): Promise<Project.PatchResult>; // adaptive icon inset; ios => empty result
native.project.detectPageAgent(): Promise<{ agent: boolean; file?: string }>; // editor agent in web.dist .js files?
native.project.checkShellLinked(opts: { target: MobileTarget; profile?: BuildProfile }): Promise<void>; // throws when the shell is composed but not linked
native.project.resolveDerivedPath(target: string): string; // the comparable real-path form every containment guard uses
native.project.clearMobileBuildOutput(opts: { target: MobileTarget }): Promise<{ removed: readonly string[] }>; // ios → gen/apple/build, android → nothing
native.project.ensureIconSource(): Promise<string>;             // app.icon, else a generated placeholder PNG
native.project.clean(opts?: { target?: Target }): Promise<{ removed: readonly string[] }>;
native.project.resolve<K extends keyof CapabilityConfigMap>(name: K, config?: CapabilityConfigMap[K]): Project.ResolvedCapability;
native.project.isKnownCapability(name: string): name is keyof CapabilityConfigMap;
native.project.getRegistryRows(): ReadonlyArray<Project.RegistryRow>;
native.project.getRequiredFiles(opts: { target: MobileTarget }): readonly string[];

// tauri (the only subprocess seam; one-shot verbs throw TauriError on non-zero exit)
native.tauri.icon(opts: { source: string }): Promise<Tauri.RunResult>;   // always --output <projectDir>/src-tauri/icons
native.tauri.build(opts: { target: Target; simulator?: boolean; aab?: boolean; exportMethod?: AppleExportMethod; onTick?: (t: Tauri.CompileTick) => void; onOutput?: (line: string) => void; env?: Readonly<Record<string, string>> }): Promise<Tauri.RunResult>; // env merged over the inherited one; never changes argv (no --debug: the debug profile is a release build)
native.tauri.mobileInit(opts: { target: "ios" | "android" }): Promise<Tauri.RunResult>; // NOT idempotent — gate on completeness() first
native.tauri.dev(opts: { target?: Target; onOutput?: (line: string) => void }): Promise<Tauri.DevHandle>;
native.tauri.getVersion(): Promise<{ cliVersion: string } | undefined>;  // undefined = CLI not invokable (never throws)
native.tauri.getRunner(): { nodePath: string; tauriJsPath: string }; // feeds project.patchMobile

// doctor (never throws on check failures; rejected checks become internal-error "fail" rows)
native.doctor.run(opts?: { target?: Target }): Promise<Doctor.DoctorReport>; // { ok, checks } — warn never flips ok

await native.stop();
```

Key types:

```ts
type Target = "macos" | "windows" | "linux" | "ios" | "android";
type NativePhase = "scaffold" | "codegen" | "icons" | "compile" | "bundle" | "collect";

type Config = {
  app: {
    name: string; identifier: string; version?: string; icon?: string; category?: string; buildNumber?: string;
    orientation?: Orientation;   // build-time mobile lock; unset = "any"; no runtime lock
    backgroundColor?: string;    // "#rrggbb" | "#rrggbbaa" -> app.windows[0].backgroundColor + Android status bar icons + Android window/splash background
    adaptiveIconInset?: number;  // Android adaptive icon inset, percent per side (0 < n <= 30); 19.44 = 66 dp safe zone
    keepScreenOn?: boolean;      // iOS: the app turns the idle timer off at launch; Android keeps it on from the page
  };
  web: { build: string; devCommand: string; devUrl: string; dist: string; cwd?: string };
  system: ReadonlyArray<{ name: string }>;
  capabilities: Partial<CapabilityConfigMap>;
  targets: readonly Target[];   // default hostTargets(process.platform) — mobile is opt-in
  projectDir: string;           // default ".moku/tauri"
  outDir: string;               // default "dist-native"
  signing: SigningConfig;
  ios?: {
    infoPlist?: Readonly<Record<string, PlistValue>>; // merged into Info.plist; app.orientation wins a shared key
    privacyManifest?: string;   // absolute path, carried as PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy; unset removes a stale one
  };
};

type PlistValue = string | boolean | readonly PlistValue[] | { readonly [key: string]: PlistValue };

type CapabilityConfigMap = {
  store: Record<string, never>;
  notification: Record<string, never>;
  "clipboard-manager": Record<string, never>;
  tray: Record<string, never>;
  "deep-link": { mode: "scheme"; scheme: string };
  back: Record<string, never>;
  haptics: Record<string, never>;
  shell: Record<string, never>;   // the Android page bridge; composed by naming it in `system`
};

type Orientation = "portrait" | "landscape" | "any";

type AppleExportMethod = "app-store-connect" | "release-testing" | "debugging";

type AppleSigning = {
  teamId?: string;                  // bundle.iOS.developmentTeam
  signingIdentity?: string;         // bundle.macOS.signingIdentity ("-" = ad-hoc)
  providerShortName?: string;       // bundle.macOS.providerShortName
  entitlements?: string;            // consumer plist, relative to cwd
  appStore?: boolean;               // generate a sandbox Entitlements.plist when `entitlements` is unset (macos)
  exportMethod?: AppleExportMethod; // tauri ios build --export-method
  macosMinimumSystemVersion?: string;
  iosMinimumSystemVersion?: string; // default "15.0" (Tauri's 14.0 is refused by Xcode 27)
};

type SigningConfig = {
  apple?: AppleSigning;
  android?: { keystorePath?: string; keystorePasswordEnv?: string; keyPasswordEnv?: string; keyAlias?: string };
  windows?: { certificateThumbprint?: string };
};

type Events = {
  "native:phase": { target: Target; phase: NativePhase; status: "start" | "progress" | "done" | "error"; durationMs?: number; detail?: string };
  "native:complete": { target: Target; outPath: string; artifacts: readonly string[]; durationMs: number; profile: BuildProfile };
};

type BuildFlavor = { simulator?: boolean | undefined; aab?: boolean | undefined; debug?: boolean | undefined };
type BuildProfile = "store" | "debug" | "dev";

// per-plugin (doctor)
type CheckResult = { id: string; target: Target | "host"; status: "pass" | "warn" | "fail"; message: string; fixIt?: string };

type DevHandle = { url: string; ready: Promise<void>; exited: Promise<{ code: number | null; signal: string | null }>; stop(): Promise<void> };

class TauriError extends Error {
  kind: "toolchain-missing" | "platform-missing" | "config-invalid" | "compile-failed"
      | "xcode-script-failed" | "signing-failed" | "device-unavailable" | "cancelled" | "unknown";
  exitCode: number | null;
  stderrTail: string; // already scrubbed — signal lines, a "…" separator, then the last 10 lines
}

type BuildResult = { target: Target; outPath: string; artifacts: readonly string[]; durationMs: number; phases: ReadonlyArray<{ phase: NativePhase; durationMs: number }>; profile: BuildProfile }; // always six phases; outPath <outDir>/<target>-debug in debug
```

Config defaults (framework `defaultConfig`): `app: { name: "", identifier: "" }` (must be set; validated), `web: { build: "bun run build", devCommand: "bun run dev", devUrl: "http://localhost:5173", dist: "dist" }`, `system: []`, `capabilities: {}`, `targets: hostTargets(process.platform)` (darwin→["macos"], win32→["windows"], linux→["linux"], other→[]), `projectDir: ".moku/tauri"`, `outDir: "dist-native"`, `signing: {}`.

Per-plugin configs (each plugin's own defaults; overridable via `createApp({ pluginConfigs })`):
- `tauri: { spawnImpl?: SpawnFn; nodePath?: string; arch?: NodeJS.Architecture; readiness: { intervalMs: number; timeoutMs: number } }` — defaults: undefined / undefined / undefined / `{ intervalMs: 250, timeoutMs: 60_000 }`. `arch` decides the iOS simulator slice (`x64` → `x86_64`, else `<arch>-sim`); undefined reads `process.arch`, and tests pin it so an argv assertion never depends on the host.
- `doctor: { probeImpl?: ProbeFn; probeTimeoutMs: number }` — defaults: undefined / `10_000` (a check that outruns the budget yields a warn).
- `cli: { renderImpl?: (line: string) => void; confirmImpl?: (question: string) => Promise<boolean> }` — defaults undefined (branded console + styled confirm from `@moku-labs/common/cli`).
- `env` (core, seeded in `src/config.ts`): `{ providers: [workerSafeProcessEnv()] }`. Core-plugin config is a SHALLOW merge, so supplying `providers` REPLACES this list: re-add `workerSafeProcessEnv()` or `ctx.env.get("PATH")` goes undefined and every build fails with `[native] Could not locate a \`node\` binary on PATH.` (The typed `createApp` pluginConfigs map covers regular plugins only; the kernel still merges an `env` key at runtime.)

## Signing and store builds

Config holds identifiers and env-var NAMES. Secrets stay in the environment and Tauri reads them itself: `APPLE_ID` + `APPLE_PASSWORD` + `APPLE_TEAM_ID`, or `APPLE_API_KEY` + `APPLE_API_ISSUER` + `APPLE_API_KEY_PATH` (either complete set satisfies doctor), plus `APPLE_CERTIFICATE` + `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` for a CI keychain. Android passwords are read by Gradle via `System.getenv("<keystorePasswordEnv>")` / `System.getenv("<keyPasswordEnv ?? keystorePasswordEnv>")` from the `// MOKU-SIGNING-START…END` block `patchMobile` maintains in `gen/android/app/build.gradle.kts` (no `keystore.properties` is written; dropping `keystorePath` removes the block). `signing.apple.appStore === true` with `entitlements` unset generates `src-tauri/Entitlements.plist` (app-sandbox + network-client) for macOS. Unsigned dev builds and iOS simulator builds need NO credentials at all — doctor's signing check is warn-only for exactly that reason.

## iOS simulator

`native.cli.build({ target: "ios", simulator: true })` → `tauri ios build --target aarch64-sim` (`x86_64`, with no `-sim` suffix, on an Intel host — set `pluginConfigs.tauri.arch` to pin it), never `--export-method`, and `collect` matches `gen/apple/build/*-sim/*.app` plus `gen/apple/build/x86_64/*.app` (a DIRECTORY, copied recursively) instead of `gen/apple/build/**/*.ipa`. Prerequisites, all checked by `native doctor`: rust targets `aarch64-apple-ios` + `aarch64-apple-ios-sim` (`rustup target add …`), `xcodegen` (`brew install xcodegen`), `pod` (`brew install cocoapods`) — the `ios-tools` check, fail posture — and an installed iOS platform/simulator runtime (`xcodebuild -downloadPlatform iOS`) — the `ios-platform` check, warn posture. The first iOS build runs `tauri ios init` once and then rewrites the runner Tauri baked into `gen/apple/project.yml` and `gen/apple/*.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` to the absolute `"<node>" "<tauri.js>"` pair — the detected `node tauri`/`bun tauri` command does not resolve inside Xcode. A path-qualified runner (`/opt/homebrew/bin/node tauri`) is matched from its first `/` — the optional path prefix never contains a quote or a backslash — so the `"` that opens the pbxproj `shellScript = "…"` string survives and the FIRST build passes. The generated `lib.rs` carries a `.setup` hook that sets the WKWebView scroll view's `contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior` to `.never` on the `main` window (via an iOS-only `objc2 = "0.6"` dependency in a `[target.'cfg(target_os = "ios")'.dependencies]` table), so the page gets the full screen while CSS `env(safe-area-inset-*)` still reports the notch; the hook is `#[cfg(target_os = "ios")]`, so lib.rs is the same file on every target. With `app.keepScreenOn` the same closure also calls `UIApplication.sharedApplication.setIdleTimerDisabled(true)`, because iOS refuses `navigator.wakeLock` until the first tap; unset, lib.rs is unchanged. REBUILDS of the same tree need two more things, both handled: `patchMobile` also writes `CODE_SIGN_ALLOW_ENTITLEMENTS_MODIFICATION = YES;` into every `buildSettings` block of the pbxproj and `CODE_SIGN_ALLOW_ENTITLEMENTS_MODIFICATION: true` under each target's `settings.base` in project.yml (a build script rewrites the entitlements file mid-build, which Xcode otherwise refuses), and the compile phase clears `gen/apple/build` first (Tauri renames its fresh `.app` into the previous archive: `Directory not empty (os error 66)`). Android needs neither — Gradle owns its build tree. A KEPT tree follows the config: `tauri ios build` never runs xcodegen on it, so a change to `project.yml` alone reaches no build, and every `patchMobile` writes `iosMinimumSystemVersion ?? "15.0"` into `deploymentTarget.iOS` in project.yml and every `IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` in project.pbxproj (a file without such a line is a `[native]` error). With `ios.privacyManifest` it copies the file's bytes to `gen/apple/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` and names it in the first `sources:` under `targets:` in project.yml and with four pbxproj lines on two fixed ids (`PBXBuildFile`, `PBXFileReference`, the `children` of the group `mainGroup` names, the `PBXResourcesBuildPhase` `files`). Each pass drops those lines first, so it is idempotent and an unset option removes them and the file, down to the original bytes. A missing source is refused before anything is written; an anchor the pbxproj lacks is a `[native]` error.

## Store builds

Every generated Cargo.toml carries `[profile.release]` (`codegen-units = 1`, `lto = true`, `opt-level = "s"`, `panic = "abort"`, `strip = true`), on every target and in every build profile. A store build sets `build.removeUnusedCommands: true` in tauri.conf.json; a debug build leaves it out. An android build with `app.buildNumber` writes `bundle.android.versionCode` as a JSON number, `{}` otherwise; anything but a whole number from 1 to 2100000000 is refused at generate, on android only, because `"1.0.3"` stays a legal macOS/iOS bundle version and `build.run({ targets })` may name a target outside `config.targets`. `ios.infoPlist` merges into `Info.ios.plist` after the capabilities and before the orientation lock, which wins a shared key; nested `<dict>` and `<array>` render.

## Breaking changes (this release)

| What breaks | Migration |
|---|---|
| `web.dev.command` / `web.dev.url` | flat `web.devCommand` / `web.devUrl` |
| `tauri.mobileInit({ platform })` | `tauri.mobileInit({ target })` |
| `Build`/`Cli`/`Doctor`/`Project`/`Tauri` namespaces are type-only | `import { TauriError } from "@moku-labs/native"` |
| default `targets` is the host desktop target, not all five | set `targets` explicitly for `ios`/`android` |
| `Project.RegistryRow` plugin fields optional (`tray` is a cargo feature) | null-check `npmPackage`/`crate`/`rustInit` |

The store-build fields are additive. One earlier stop: a non-numeric `app.buildNumber` on an android build is refused at generate, where Tauri would have failed on it anyway. `Project.PlistValue` widens to the recursive `PlistValue`.

## File Structure

```
src/
  config.ts               # Layer 1: Config/Events types, TARGETS, PHASE_ORDER, hostTargets,
                          #   CapabilityConfigMap, SigningConfig/AppleSigning, MobileTarget/TauriRunner/BuildFlavor/BuildProfile,
                          #   createCoreConfig("native") + the env provider seed
  index.ts                # Layer 2: createCore(...5 plugins) — no pluginConfigs; public exports:
                          #   createApp, createPlugin, constants, TauriError, types, plugin barrel
  plugins/
    index.ts              # barrel: plugin instances + TYPE-ONLY namespaces (Project, Tauri, Build, Doctor, Cli)
    project/              # Complex tier
      index.ts types.ts api.ts validate.ts layout.ts paths.ts registry.ts writer.ts clean.ts icon.ts
      orientation.ts xml.ts page-agent.ts
      mobile/             # completeness.ts files.ts signing.ts manifest.ts system-bars.ts runner.ts
                          #   xcode-settings.ts ios-project.ts profile.ts icon.ts shell-link.ts patch.ts (orchestration only)
      generators/         # tauri-conf.ts cargo.ts rust.ts capabilities.ts build-script.ts
                          #   entitlements.ts sidecar.ts paths.ts types.ts
        shell/            # the tauri-plugin-moku-shell crate: index.ts rust.ts page-script.ts android.ts
    tauri/                # Standard tier
      index.ts types.ts api.ts argv.ts resolve.ts spawn.ts dev.ts stream.ts errors.ts scrub.ts state.ts
    build/                # Standard tier
      index.ts types.ts api.ts pipeline.ts collect.ts   # layout via project.getBundleLayout
    doctor/               # Complex tier
      index.ts types.ts api.ts report.ts
      checks/             # index.ts types.ts rustup.ts node.ts xcode.ts ios-tools.ts ios-platform.ts
                          #   android.ts android-platform.ts android-debug-signing.ts signing.ts
                          #   completeness.ts versions.ts web-script.ts
                          #   tauri-cli.ts cross-repo.ts
    cli/                  # Standard tier
      index.ts types.ts api.ts handlers.ts render.ts state.ts
tests/                    # framework-level integration only; plugin tests are colocated in
                          #   src/plugins/<name>/__tests__/{unit,integration}/
  smoke/                  # real-toolchain proof — `bun run test:smoke` only, never `bun run test`
                          #   composes all five capabilities, then LAUNCHES the built macOS
                          #   binary: a config the plugins reject builds fine, dies on frame 1
```

## Plugins

- **project** — Capability registry + `.moku/tauri` generators (tauri.conf.json, Cargo.toml with cargo features + the iOS-only objc2 table, build.rs, main.rs/lib.rs with the iOS safe-area hook, capability JSON, Entitlements.plist, Info.ios.plist sidecar) + write-if-changed writer + mobile completeness gate + the mobile patch pass (Android: signing block → main-activity manifest attributes such as `android:screenOrientation` → runner rewrite; iOS: entitlements-modification setting → deployment target → privacy manifest → runner rewrite) + the build profiles (Android: profile block → signing (debug keystore in debug) → manifest → system bars → runner) + the adaptive icon inset (patchMobileIcons) + the `tauri-plugin-moku-shell` crate generator + the editor-agent page scan + the shell link check + the build-time orientation lock + the placeholder icon + guarded clean/clearMobileBuildOutput; never spawns | tier: Complex | API: generate, getBundleLayout, getCompleteness, patchMobile, patchMobileIcons, detectPageAgent, checkShellLinked, ensureIconSource, clean, clearMobileBuildOutput, resolveDerivedPath, resolve, isKnownCapability, getRegistryRows, getRequiredFiles | events: none (onInit validates global config).
- **tauri** — The only `@tauri-apps/cli` subprocess seam: argv builders (simulator/export-method/aab), injectable spawn resolving on `close` not `exit`, extra child `env` for `build` (`MOKU_NATIVE_PROFILE`), process-group dev lifecycle with devUrl readiness poll, compile-tick stream parsing, TauriError taxonomy, entropy-gated secret scrubbing, `getRunner()`; NO onStop by design (D-002) | tier: Standard | API: icon, build, mobileInit, dev, getVersion, getRunner | events: none.
- **build** — Sequential per-target pipeline (scaffold→codegen→icons→compile→bundle→collect) plus `prepare` (first three); depends [project, tauri] resolved ONCE as deps; threads the build profile (`debug` → `"debug"` on Android and iOS, `dev` → `"dev"`, both refused) to generate/patchMobile/checkShellLinked/tauri env/collect/native:complete; refuses a store build whose page carries the editor agent (after compile, before collect); owns collect (glob table → outDir/<target>/ or outDir/<target>-debug/, simulator `.app` vs device `.ipa`, name collisions resolved by newest mtime, real-path containment via `project.resolveDerivedPath` before each destination is removed, zero matches is an error); runAll is sequential (shared Cargo target/ lock) | tier: Standard | API: prepare, run, runAll | events: emits global native:phase + native:complete.
- **doctor** — Parallel diagnosis via checks/ registry (rustup, node, xcode, ios-tools, ios-platform, android, android-platform (the `compileSdk` SDK platform installed — fail; fix-it `sdkmanager "platforms;android-N"`), android-debug-signing (the `~/.android/debug.keystore` a debug build signs with — warn; fix-it the `keytool` command), signing presence/counts, mobile completeness, npm-vs-crate version skew, web-script existence, tauri-cli, cross-repo warns); Promise.allSettled — rejected checks become internal-error fails; each check races `probeTimeoutMs` and a timeout is a warn; warns never flip `ok` | tier: Complex | API: run | events: declares + emits doctor:check per completed check, as it settles.
- **cli** — Typed verb surface (build/dev/doctor/clean), NO argv parsing; ONE branded console built in createState (`ctx.state.ui`); live progress via hooks on native:phase/native:complete/doctor:check (doctor rows print once, live; the summary is counts only; a debug delivery's completion panel reads `debug build → <outPath>`); `build` forwards `simulator`/`aab`/`debug` unchanged; a failed build prints the scrubbed `stderrTail` in a box before the error (tail lines are cut to the terminal width minus box chrome ONLY when stdout reports columns — `tailLineBound(columns)`; piped/CI output keeps every line whole); `onInit` clears the default log sink and installs a branded one (threshold `info`) bound to `ctx.state.ui`, so `ctx.log` records render as branded lines through the same seam instead of raw objects; depends on all four other plugins | tier: Standard | API: build, dev, doctor, clean | events: none declared — hooks only.

Dependency graph (D-007): project and tauri are dependency-free (Wave 1); build → [project, tauri] and doctor → [project, tauri] (Wave 2); cli → [project, tauri, build, doctor] (Wave 3). Initialization order follows the plugin array: project, tauri, build, doctor, cli.

## Minimal consumer example

```ts
// src/system.ts (shared with the web app)
export const systemPlugins = [{ name: "store" }, { name: "deep-link" }];

// src/native.ts
import { createApp } from "@moku-labs/native";
import { systemPlugins } from "./system";

export const native = createApp({
  config: {
    app: { name: "MyApp", identifier: "com.example.myapp", icon: "assets/icon.png" },
    web: { build: "bun run build", devCommand: "bun run dev", devUrl: "http://localhost:5173", dist: "dist" },
    system: systemPlugins,
    capabilities: { "deep-link": { mode: "scheme", scheme: "myapp" } },
    targets: ["macos", "ios"],              // default: the host's own desktop target
    signing: { apple: { teamId: "ABCDE12345", exportMethod: "app-store-connect" } }
  }
});

// scripts/native-build.ts
import { native } from "../src/native";
await native.start();
await native.cli.build({ target: "macos" });          // installers land in dist-native/macos/
await native.cli.build({ target: "ios", simulator: true }); // unsigned .app in dist-native/ios/
await native.cli.build({ target: "android", debug: true });   // debug profile -> dist-native/android-debug/
await native.stop();
```

Add `.moku/` and `dist-native/` to the consumer `.gitignore`. A real `node` binary on PATH is a hard prerequisite (`@tauri-apps/cli` cannot run under bun; `native doctor` checks it). Package manager: bun exclusively.

## Error handling

- Every framework error message is `[native]`-prefixed with an actionable second line (fix-it style).
- `tauri` one-shot verbs throw classified `TauriError` (kind + exitCode + scrubbed stderrTail). Kinds, most specific first: `xcode-script-failed` (the Xcode "Build Rust Code" phase), `signing-failed`, `toolchain-missing`, `platform-missing` (iOS SDK/simulator platform not installed — `xcodebuild -downloadPlatform iOS`), `device-unavailable`, `config-invalid`, `compile-failed`, `cancelled` (signal), `unknown`. The message quotes the cause line (first error among the last 15 signal lines) between the bucket and the advice. Lines matching `^\s*Warn\b` are never classified (every unsigned simulator build prints a code-signing warning).
- `build` emits `native:phase` status "error" for the OPEN phase (compile or bundle), then rethrows; later phases never start; `runAll` stops at the first failing target.
- Profile errors: `debug` and `dev` together → `[native] debug and dev cannot be combined.` before any phase; `debug` on a target other than android or ios → `[native] --debug builds Android and iOS only for now (asked for <target>).` before any phase; a store build whose page carries the editor agent → `[native] store build refused: the page carries the editor agent (<dist>/<file>).` / `Build with debug: true.` (open phase, nothing collected); a debug build without the SDK debug keystore → `[native] debug keystore not found at <path>.` + the `keytool` command (codegen); the shell composed but not linked → `[native] the shell plugin is not linked into gen/android …` (clean android and rebuild).
- `doctor.run` never throws on check failures — a rejected check becomes a `"fail"` CheckResult with an internal-error message; a timed-out check becomes a `"warn"`.
- `cli.dev` resolves cleanly on signal-terminated exits (code null, e.g. Ctrl-C) and throws only on a numeric non-zero exit code.
- `cli.clean()` without a target gates the full projectDir wipe behind a styled confirm; declining resolves without deleting. `clean()` itself refuses an unsafe `projectDir` (the project anchor, cwd, `$HOME`, a filesystem root, or an ancestor of any of them).
- Config validation (project.onInit, composition time): empty app.name, non-reverse-DNS app.identifier, missing web.build/web.devCommand/web.devUrl/web.dist, app.backgroundColor not `#rrggbb`/`#rrggbbaa`, app.orientation outside "portrait"/"landscape"/"any", app.adaptiveIconInset not a finite number with 0 < n ≤ 30, signing.apple.iosMinimumSystemVersion not `MAJOR.MINOR[.PATCH]`, a relative ios.privacyManifest, an ios.infoPlist value (nested too) that is not a string, boolean, array or plain object, unknown config.system names, deep-link composed without a scheme.

See llms-full.txt for verbatim type definitions, the full config/event catalog, per-check details, and extension patterns. Per-plugin READMEs: src/plugins/{project,tauri,build,doctor,cli}/README.md.
